questions.question: Ability to adapt to the new cultural value system f. Edward T Hall g. Geert Hofstede h. cultural relativism i. Enculturation j. acculturation II. IIA. Categorize the following words as American and British English based on their spelling variation: MODELING, CENTRE, TYRE, PROGRAMME (02) II B. Choose the right answer to fill in the blanks for the following: (02) a. An American would always check the …………………..of the taxi. i. Number plate ii. License plate b. If you are a British, you would ask for a ……………… i. Plaster ii. Band-Aid c. A British would always carry his/her ……………in the front pocket. i. Purse ii. Wallet d. If you are an American student, you wish to live in a reasonable……….. i. Flat ii. Apartment Page 2 of 4 III. Analyze the following case on the basis of your understanding of Edward Hall’s theory of communication styles: (07) Mr. Brian, an American, has just joined as the Head of Operations of the Indian Branch of a large multinational firm. While reviewing the projects currently being implemented, he notices a big problem with one of them. This particular project is running way behind schedule and there have also been large over-runs in terms of cost. After making preliminary enquiries he writes a letter to the Project Manager enquiring the reasons for delay and asking for the proposed date of completionof the project. The Project Manager Mr. Sathish knew that there was a problem in completion of the project due to some pending permissions. The permissions needed to be cleared by the Finance Executive, but the Finance Executive was keeping them on hold as he did not have good relations with the earlier Head of Operations of the firm. Mr. Sathish sends a letter to Mr. Brian stating that he was sorry for the delay but would try his best to overcome such problems in future. He also states that the Finance Executive needs to be informed of the delay and it is better to meet the Finance Executive in person. Mr. Brian feels that Mr. Sathish has not answered his queries properly as he has given no reasons for the delay and not specified the proposed date of completion. Further, he could not understand why he needs to meet the Finance Executive. He feels that Satish is avoiding the responsibility. Brian summons Sathish and tells him to get the work done immediately. Sathish looks down and nods his head. Brian asks Sathish if he faces any specific problems in getting the work done, for which Sathish shakes his head and promises to do his best. Brian seems puzzled as Sathish walks out of the room silently without submitting any concrete plans. He feels that Sathish does not want to work under him for some reasons. Questions: • What are the reasons for miscommunication? • What are your suggestions to avoid such miscommunication in future? IV. Analyze the following case in terms of your understanding of Hofstede’s Theory on Intercultural Communication. What different cultural dimensions operate in the following society? (08) A team of managers is meeting to set up a new project team. One of the people being considered is a woman and one of the men says that he heard that the woman being considered was pregnant. The team leader, Mr. Stevan, is of the opinion that the woman in question is a competent person and her inputs may enhance the efficiency, and help them to get better results. Yet, he wants to take a decision on this based on the majority view and asks the members to express their views. One of the members, Mr. Paul stated that because the project was very time-sensitive, he saw no point in involving the woman as it may affect their performance if she is not able to give Page 3 of 4 her time later. A number of male managers seem to agree with the opinion and feel that they may not able to complete the target if there is a change in the team halfway through. Ms. Reema, a female member is of the view that as the immediate monetary incentives completely depends on the quality of the project, they should think carefully before taking any risk. Overall, the members feel that the team leader should consider the completion of the project in a successful way as a priority. V. Analyze the following on the basis of your understanding of non-verbal communication across cultures: (06) An Indian supervisor in a multinational firm calls in the Japanese employee for an annual evaluation. The supervisor smiles as the employee walks in and offers him a seat. After the supervisor offers some positive aspects of the evaluation, she begins to discuss areas for improvement. The Japanese employee looks down at the floor during the entire feedback session, and starts to smile when areas for improvement are mentioned. The supervisor concludes that the employee is not happy with the feedback. When the supervisor tries to draw it out of him, the employee continues to smile. The supervisor finds the whole situation confusing and insists that the employee must reveal the secret. • How might this behavior be explained? What do you think is taking place? VI. Choose the right answer to the following case and give three reasons as to why you have chosen it: (04) You have just been posted to Germany and are now the head of the production team that involves local employees. You found that the team members had made a number of mistakes and the work needs a complete revision. You plan to suggest certain new policies to enhance the performance. In the next meeting as a team leader you would A. Review the steps involved with the whole team and suggest the measures to overcome them B. Ask each team member to speak out about the problems faced, and you point out the mistakes made by them and discuss the possible changes C. Read out the new policy to be followed by every member VII. Answer ANY TWO of the following in about 10^0 words: (2 × 6= 12)
